title: UK public sector finances, August 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the boundary print for the Budget's forecast, and the quietest kind of day the gilt tape has
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/publicsectorfinancesukaugust2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — reads verbatim 'Public sector finances, UK: August 2026', 'Release date: 22 September 2026 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', 'These are accredited official statistics'. CORROBORATED FROM A SECOND, INDEPENDENT PUBLISHER PRIMARY the same session: the ONS's live PSF bulletin (July 2026 data, published 2026-08-21, fetched direct HTTP 200) names its own 'Next release: 22 September 2026'. Cadence independently reproduced from the publisher's own past-release listing, scraped direct across eight pages: 80 consecutive PSF bulletins from 2020-01-22 to 2026-08-21 fall on the 19th-26th of the month, 80 of 80, with no outlier and never a Monday; 25 of the 80 are Tuesdays and 2026-09-22 is a Tuesday. The gov.uk statutory pre-announcement register 404'd on the expected slug (recorded in the ledger's probe-ref.blocked, not substituted), so this rests on two ONS primaries plus cadence rather than on a register entry. Filed estimate on the taxonomy gap (market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix list has no slot for a foreign national statistics institute) and this lane's no-self-confirm limit — the DATE is not in doubt. Proposed 2026-09-09 by the uk-public-sector-finances-2026-10-21 lane; researched and made canonical by its own lane the same day
notes: RESEARCHED 2026-09-09 by its own lane (docs/research/events/uk-public-sector-finances-2026-09-22.md), which re-fetched every primary rather than inheriting the proposer's. It supersedes proposals/uk-public-sector-finances-2026-09-22.from-uk-public-sector-finances-2026-10-21.json, now inert. TITLE AMENDED on two findings. (1) PLACEMENT — this is the BOUNDARY print for the 2026-10-28 Budget's OBR forecast, not comfortably inside it. Two OBR precedents put the pre-measures forecast 34-36 days ahead of the fiscal event: the October 2024 EFO's was 'finalised on 26 September' (34d before 2024-10-30) and the November 2025 fiscal forecast's determinants closed over the ten working days to 2025-10-21 (36d before 2025-11-26). 2026-09-22 is EXACTLY 36 days before 2026-10-28 — inside on the 2024 convention with two days to spare, and exactly on the line on the 2025 one. The 2024 analogue print (August data, published 2024-09-20) had six days of margin; this one has zero to two. Both precedents are SEARCH RELAYS — obr.uk returned 403 to this lane twice, recorded — so the placement is registered as FT-uk-public-sector-finances-2026-09-22-1 rather than asserted. (2) THE MARKET HALF IS A MEASURED NULL, AND THE RE-BASING PRINTS ARE THE QUIETEST OF ALL. First-party study against this repo's market-data layer: across 70 PSF release days since 2020-11-20, IGLT.L moved 1.14x an ordinary day (Welch t = 1.02), GBP/USD 0.88x, US 10y 0.90x, FTSE 100 0.92x, SPY 1.03x — five series, five nulls, independently reproducing the sibling 10-21 lane's numbers. On the FIVE September releases that carry the annual data updates — the class this print belongs to — IGLT.L moved 0.210% mean absolute against a 0.427% control: 0.49x an ordinary day (t = -2.86) and 0.43x a PSF day (t = -2.94), with all five moves at or under 0.38% against a p90 of 0.900%. The re-basing is a READING event, not a pricing one. n = 5 is the honest limit. THE 2026 CORRIDOR IS CLEANER THAN THE SAMPLE, not dirtier: all five historical September PSF prints landed within two days of a September FOMC decision (federalreserve.gov's own calendar: 2021-09-22, 2022-09-21, 2023-09-20, 2024-09-18, 2025-09-17), which is why FTSE and US 10y run hot on those days while gilts run cold; in 2026 the FOMC is 2026-09-16, SIX days earlier, the widest gap in the sample. UNLIKE ITS 10-21 SIBLING THERE IS NO CO-PRINT: UK CPI for August 2026 publishes 2026-09-16 07:00 (separate ONS page, fetched direct), six days before, so no attribution hazard attaches to this morning. WHAT THIS PRINT ACTUALLY DOES: the ONS's July 2026 bulletin states that the September 2026 release carries the regular annual data updates — pension fund liability estimates, equity valuation in multilateral development banks, central government lease modelling, and the Scottish National Investment Bank's classification into the UK public sector — so it re-bases the LEVEL of the series every later bulletin, including the 10-21 one, is read against. Live baseline it replaces: borrowing £1.8bn in July 2026 (+£0.7bn y/y, +£2.3bn vs OBR), FY-to-July £56.7bn (-£6.0bn/9.6% y/y, +£2.3bn vs the OBR's March 2026 EFO), debt 94.1% of GDP, CGNCR £2.8bn (+£3.9bn vs OBR). NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED: symbols [], this repo tracks no UK-listed name, and no house playbook is fiscal-, rates- or sterling-keyed; the gilt-to-Treasury pipe the Budget lane measured (-6.08bp of US 10y per +1% IGLT.L, t = -45.3, n = 4610) opens only on the worst 1% of gilt days (<= -1.30%), and no September PSF print in five years has produced anything past 0.38%. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
